harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured, enabled, and verified inventory-database and inventory-api as systemd services on node1. The API requires the database and starts only after its readiness marker is present. Both services recovered successfully after a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Created inventory-database.service with stale-marker cleanup, readiness waiting, failure restart, and shutdown cleanup.
Created inventory-api.service with Requires/After dependencies and a readiness precheck.
Verified ordered startup from a marker-absent state and dependent shutdown when the database stopped.
Restarted node1 safely and confirmed its boot identity changed and both services recovered.

evidence.requirement: Manage both supplied programs as enabled services
evidence.summary: The unit files validate successfully, are enabled, and remained installed after reboot.

evidence.requirement: API starts only after the database is ready
evidence.summary: The supplied readiness contract was identified; starting the API with no marker started the database first, completed its readiness check, then passed the API precheck. Current-boot journal timestamps independently show database startup preceding API startup.

evidence.requirement: API does not remain active without its database
evidence.summary: Stopping the database made both services inactive and removed the readiness marker.

Captured healthy baseline under boot ID 6001d24d-a752-4a58-a0b2-082876564497, received safe reboot acknowledgement, observed new boot ID cb7f3aa7-8e45-433d-a326-05e2e9f0fec7, and confirmed both enabled services, readiness state, and live processes recovered with no failed units.
